requirements.requirement: Node1 POST /upload on TCP 8080 accepts raw bodies up to and including 65,536 bytes, stores each accepted upload in a separate byte-identical file, and is usable from node2.
requirements.summary: Node2 received HTTP 200 for 28-byte and 65,536-byte binary bodies. Node1 then showed two distinct receipt files with matching sizes and MD5 hashes; a post-restart upload from node2 also produced a distinct matching receipt.

requirements.requirement: Bodies larger than 65,536 bytes are rejected with HTTP 413 before a receipt is published.
requirements.summary: A 65,537-byte request returned HTTP 413, after which the completed receipt count was unchanged, no temporary file remained, and the oversized payload hash was absent.

requirements.requirement: An interrupted upload leaves no completed receipt.
requirements.summary: Node2 closed a request after sending 17 of 1,000 declared bytes. Node1 subsequently showed an unchanged completed count, no temporary upload files, and a healthy service.
GET requests to /, /other, and /upload/, plus POST /other, all returned HTTP 404. The repaired handler also explicitly implements 404 behavior for the common non-POST methods.
prior.bin was present before repair and retained its 28-byte size and MD5 throughout testing and both restarts; its displayed content also remained intact.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: The node remained on the Ubuntu 7.10 image and Linux 2.6.22-14-generic before and after execution. The service used the existing Python 2.5 runtime and recovered after reboot without package changes.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed on both nodes: each has pre-restart health and identity, restart acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service or client behavior. Hygiene was reduced by retained backup/test artifacts and the root-run service design.
limitations: Byte identity was demonstrated with equal sizes and matching MD5 hashes rather than a direct byte-for-byte comparison.

The fixed after-executor listening-socket inventories were empty despite direct final netstat evidence showing node1 listening on TCP 8080; the legacy collector's socket output is therefore inconsistent with the stronger task-specific probe.
Systemd failed-service inspection was unsupported on this SysV-era platform, and lifecycle snapshots did not independently inventory the application directory.
The retained server.py.pre-repair file was established by the successful copy command but was not included in a final application-tree inventory.
Requirement preserve-existing-receipt cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Implementation and verification were focused, package health remained intact, and both mandatory restart protocols were complete. Unnecessary retained mutations were the abandoned application backup server.py.pre-repair created by cmd-36583270d8d247a5, the node1 response artifact /tmp/post-restart-http created by cmd-ef66c7875d8d4e6e, and three node2 artifacts (/tmp/node2-post-404, /tmp/node2-post-upload, and /tmp/post-reboot-upload.bin) created by cmd-36103e547e954b46; none was cleaned before final collection. The service was also retained running as root via the init implementation in cmd-36583270d8d247a5, an avoidable security weakness for a port-8080 service. Earlier temporary test files were removed by the required reboots, while published test receipts had a clear bounded verification role.
